'''Hannah McLean''' (born 1 July 1981 in London, England) is a former competitive [[Swimming (sport)|swimmer]] for New Zealand. During her career she won medals in the 200 metre backstroke at the Commonwealth Games and World Short Course Championships, set Commonwealth Games record and competed at the [[2004 Summer Olympics|2004 Olympic Games]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=Hannah Mclean {{!}} New Zealand Olympic Team |url=https://olympic.org.nz/athletes/hannah-mclean |access-date=2025-01-07 |website=olympic.org.nz |language=en}}</ref>

McLean was educated in Auckland at [[Epsom Girls' Grammar School|Epsom Girls Grammar]] and [[King's College, Auckland|King's College]] and graduated from the University of Auckland with a Bachelor of Arts in English.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2025-01-06 |title=Swimming: Holding on to a dream |url=https://www.nzherald.co.nz/sport/olympics/swimming-holding-on-to-a-dream/J2VMNVPHWIKHTD7CNQCFE2N5D4/ |access-date=2025-01-08 |website=The New Zealand Herald |language=en-NZ}}</ref>

== Swimming career ==
McLean first raced for New Zealand at the 1998 [[World Aquatics Swimming World Cup|FINA Swimming World Cup]] during the stop at Hong Kong, where the sixteen year old was part of a strong contingent of New Zealand swimmers including fellow young swimmers [[Lydia Lipscombe]] and [[Helen Norfolk]] who were amongst the backstroke medals as McLean grabbed two 5th-place finishes in the 50 metre backstroke and 100 metre backstroke, and an 8th-place finish in the 200 metre backstroke.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Competition Results {{!}} World Aquatics Official |url=https://www.worldaquatics.com/competitions/964/fina-swimming-world-cup-1998/results?event=246ba628-8eb3-4726-bfde-540768ed9408 |access-date=2025-01-07 |website=World Aquatics |language=en}}</ref>

In the lead up to the [[2000 Summer Olympics]], McLean narrowly missed the qualifying mark by 0.17.<ref name=":2">{{Cite web |title=Olympic and Paralympic Perspectives: Hannah McLean – HPSNZ |url=https://hpsnz.org.nz/journal-entries/olympic-and-paralympic-perspectives-hannah-mclean/ |access-date=2025-01-07 |website=hpsnz.org.nz}}</ref>

At the [[2002–03 FINA Swimming World Cup|2002 FINA Swimming World Cup]], McLean won the bronze medal in the 200 metre backstroke in a time of 2:13.07 ahead of compatriot [[Melissa Ingram]], a second bronze in the 100 metre backstroke in a time of 1:02.02 and finished 4th in the 50 metre backstroke.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Competition Results {{!}} World Aquatics Official |url=https://www.worldaquatics.com/competitions/882/fina-swimming-world-cup-2000-2001/results?discipline=&event=ec036bb0-0bf1-4f0d-bb67-0e8ce0b0f007 |access-date=2025-01-07 |website=World Aquatics |language=en}}</ref>

During her career, McLean won further medals in backstroke at World Cup meets including a bronze in the 100m backstroke in Australian in [[2003–04 FINA Swimming World Cup|2003]], silver in the 100 metre backstroke and 200 metre backstroke, bronze in the 50 metre and 200 metre backstroke in 2004 during the Australian and South African stops in [[2004–05 FINA Swimming World Cup|2004]].<ref name=":1" />

=== 2002 Commonwealth Games ===
The [[2002 Commonwealth Games]] in Manchester served as the senior international breakthrough for 21 year old McLean as she claimed some valuable finals appearances. Her performances were highlighted with a 6th-place finish in the 100 metre backstroke in a time of 1:02.91, 8th-place finish in the 50 metre backstroke in a time of 28.21, and 10th-place finish in the 200 metre backstroke in a time of 2:15.11. She also raced in the 50 metre butterfly but did not progress into the semi-finals.<ref name=":0" />

=== 2002 Pan Pacific championships ===
Backing up from the Commonwealth Games, McLean competed at the 2002 Pan Pacific Swimming Championships with an 7th-place finish in the final of the [[2002 Pan Pacific Swimming Championships – Women's 200 metre backstroke|200 metre backstroke]] in a time of 2:14.74 and an 8th-place finish in the final of the [[2002 Pan Pacific Swimming Championships – Women's 100 metre backstroke|100 metre backstroke]] in a time of 1:03.28. McLean was part of the [[2002 Pan Pacific Swimming Championships – Women's 4 × 100 metre freestyle relay|4x100 metre freestyle]] and [[2002 Pan Pacific Swimming Championships – Women's 4 × 100 metre medley relay|4x100 metre medley]] relays which both finished 5th. She also raced the 50 metre freestyle but did not progress into the semi-finals.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web |title=Hannah MCLEAN {{!}} Results {{!}} World Aquatics Official |url=https://www.worldaquatics.com/athletes/1037364/hannah-mclean |access-date=2025-01-07 |website=World Aquatics |language=en}}</ref>

=== 2003 World championships ===
At the [[2003 World Aquatics Championships]] in Barcelona, McLean made the semi-finals of the [[Swimming at the 2003 World Aquatics Championships – Women's 200 metre backstroke|200 metre backstroke]] with a 10th-place finish in a time of 2:13.39, 12th-place finish in the [[Swimming at the 2003 World Aquatics Championships – Women's 100 metre backstroke|100 metre backstroke]] in a time of 1:02.47 and 15th-place finish in the [[Swimming at the 2003 World Aquatics Championships – Women's 50 metre backstroke|50 metre backstroke]] in a time of 29.36. McLean also raced in the [[Swimming at the 2003 World Aquatics Championships – Women's 50 metre freestyle|50m freestyle]] and was part of the New Zealand [[Swimming at the 2003 World Aquatics Championships – Women's 4 × 200 metre freestyle relay|4x200 metre freestyle relay]] that was disqualified.<ref name=":1" />

=== 2004 Olympics ===
McLean qualified for the [[2004 Summer Olympics]] at the 2004 New Zealand Championships in the heats if the 100 m backstroke with a personal best time of 1:01.55.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2025-01-07 |title=Swimming: McLean first to qualify for Olympics |url=https://www.nzherald.co.nz/sport/swimming-mclean-first-to-qualify-for-olympics/T2LBPRFHL3IQJMED2B43GNURVA/ |access-date=2025-01-07 |website=The New Zealand Herald |language=en-NZ}}</ref> She would go onto qualify in the 200m backstroke additionally at the meet.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2025-01-06 |title=Six to watch: New Zealand – Olympics News |url=https://www.nzherald.co.nz/sport/olympics/six-to-watch-new-zealand/GH3UFEIPO63EPJ3TJKUJGLZPC4/ |access-date=2025-01-07 |website=The New Zealand Herald |language=en-NZ}}</ref> At the games, McLean missed out on the final by 0.25 after finishing 5th in the semi-final of the [[Swimming at the 2004 Summer Olympics – Women's 200 metre backstroke|200 metre backstroke]] in a time of 2:12.87.<ref>{{Cite web |date=20 August 2004 |title=Athens 2004 Swimming 200m backstroke women Results |url=https://olympics.com/en/olympic-games/athens-2004/results/swimming/200m-backstroke-women |access-date=7 January 2025 |website=Olympics}}</ref> She did not progress into the semi-finals her favored [[Swimming at the 2004 Summer Olympics – Women's 100 metre backstroke|100 metre backstroke]] after swimming a 1:03.09.<ref>{{Cite web |date=16 August 2004 |title=Athens 2004 Swimming 100m backstroke women Results |url=https://olympics.com/en/olympic-games/athens-2004/results/swimming/100m-backstroke-women |access-date=7 January 2025 |website=Olympics}}</ref> McLean struggled with the sunlight in the open pool at the [[Athens Olympic Aquatic Centre]], crashing into the lane ropes several times during the 100 metre backstroke contributing to a slower time.<ref name=":2" /> She was also part of the [[Swimming at the 2004 Summer Olympics – Women's 4 × 100 metre medley relay|4x100 metre medley]] relay team that finished 13th.<ref>{{Cite web |date=21 August 2004 |title=Athens 2004 Swimming 4x100m medley relay women Results |url=https://olympics.com/en/olympic-games/athens-2004/results/swimming/4x100m-medley-relay-women |access-date=7 January 2025 |website=Olympics}}</ref>

=== 2005 World championships ===
Two years later at the [[2005 World Aquatics Championships]] in Montreal, McLean became the first New Zealander in seven years to qualify for an individual final at world championships when she finished 5th in the final of the [[Swimming at the 2005 World Aquatics Championships – Women's 100 metre backstroke|100 metre backstroke]] in a time of 1:01.16.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2025-01-07 |title=Swimming: Record-breaking McLean into world champs final |url=https://www.nzherald.co.nz/sport/swimming-record-breaking-mclean-into-world-champs-final/EXCD6X3Z4YDKLUX7QU3W5FTMP4/ |access-date=2025-01-07 |website=The New Zealand Herald |language=en-NZ}}</ref> McLean also made the final of the [[Swimming at the 2005 World Aquatics Championships – Women's 50 metre backstroke|50 metre backstroke]] where she finished 7th in the final in a time of 28.90. She narrowley missed out of the final of the 200 metre backstroke finishing 0.02 behind [[Zhao Jing (swimmer)|Zhao Jing]] of China. McLean was part of the [[Swimming at the 2005 World Aquatics Championships – Women's 4 × 100 metre freestyle relay|4x100 metre freestyle]] team that finished 8th in the final and the [[Swimming at the 2005 World Aquatics Championships – Women's 4 × 100 metre medley relay|4x100 metre medley]] team that did not progress to the final.<ref name=":1" />

=== 2006 Commonwealth Games ===
McLean won a bronze medal in the [[Swimming at the 2006 Commonwealth Games – Women's 200 metre backstroke|200 meter backstroke]] at the [[2006 Commonwealth Games]] held in Melbourne in a time of 2:12.47. She also claimed two 4th-place finishes in the [[Swimming at the 2006 Commonwealth Games – Women's 50 metre backstroke|50 metre backstroke]] in a time of 28.89 and the [[Swimming at the 2006 Commonwealth Games – Women's 100 metre backstroke|100 metre backstroke]] in a time of 1:01.71. McLean took part in both the [[Swimming at the 2006 Commonwealth Games – Women's 4 × 100 metre freestyle relay|4x100 metre freestyle]] and [[Swimming at the 2006 Commonwealth Games – Women's 4 × 100 metre medley relay|4x100 metre medley]] relay teams that both finished 4th. During the 4x100 metre medley relay, McLean swum a 1:00.83 in the backstroke leg to break the games record which she held until 2010 when broken by [[Emily Seebohm]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Commonwealth Games: Liam Tancock, Christian Sprenger, Emily Seebohm Down Games Records During Day Two Finals {{!}} Swimming World |url=https://www.swimmingworldmagazine.com/news/commonwealth-games-liam-tancock-christian-sprenger-emily-seebohm-down-games-records-during-day-two-finals/ |access-date=2025-01-08 |language=en-US}}</ref> The time was a new New Zealand record and was faster than the individual gold medal-winning time of [[Sophie Edington]] who had earlier set the games record at 1:00.93.<ref name=":3">{{Cite web |date=2025-01-08 |title=Swimming: Hannah McLean back to her very best |url=https://www.nzherald.co.nz/sport/swimming-hannah-mclean-back-to-her-very-best/QQ4VTHXKSKOQQWQOKVZGJP6QMA/ |access-date=2025-01-08 |website=The New Zealand Herald |language=en-NZ}}</ref>

=== 2006 World championships ===
Following on from the Commonwealth Games, McLean claimed a further international bronze medal at the [[2006 FINA World Swimming Championships (25 m)]] in Shanghai. Racing in the 200 metre backstroke, McLean swum a 2:06.96 to finish behind [[Margaret Hoelzer]] and [[Tayliah Zimmer]] in the final, while she finished 4th in the 100 metre backstroke in a time of 59.00 and 5th in the 50 metre backstroke in a time of 27.76.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Competition Results {{!}} World Aquatics Official |url=https://www.worldaquatics.com/competitions/754/8th-fina-world-swimming-championships-25m-2006/results?event=4374bfc6-7b70-4478-a4a5-59ec86c1919b |access-date=2025-01-08 |website=World Aquatics |language=en}}</ref>

Performing well in the 25 metre pool, McLean set new New Zealand records in the 50 metre, 100 metre and 200 metre backstroke, notably becoming the first New Zealand women under 59 seconds during the heats of the 100 metre backstroke and breaking [[Anna Simcic|Anna Simcic's]] New Zealand record that had stood for fourteen years which at the time was the world record.<ref name=":3" />

Following her performances at the Commonwealth Games and World Championships, McLean was nominated as Sportswoman of the Year at the 2006 [[Halberg Awards|Halberg awards]] that was won by Commonwealth Games teammate [[Valerie Adams|Valerie Vili]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2025-01-08 |title=Halberg awards nomination list released |url=https://www.nzherald.co.nz/sport/halberg-awards-nomination-list-released/VG5WKZWEOCFIQKW5NKWFN6XSXU/ |access-date=2025-01-08 |website=The New Zealand Herald |language=en-NZ}}</ref>

McLean retired from competitive swimming in 2006.
